title: E1a grapt-engined composition root: argument admission, platform refusal, receipt custody and the single JSON receipt

owner.note: Pattern A. The validator resolves this scenario from env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR") inside the candidate tree and never calls test-support/fixtures.rs, so it imports no cross-repository read, no SECODE_FIXTURES precedence and no Linux failure mode. That is also what keeps this corpus out of the mutation profile's inputs.artifacts list: no EB witness reaches a fixture path, so a missing-input failure cannot be mistaken for a fired witness.

note: Every row drives the built binary as a caller meets it and compares the ONE JSON object it prints, byte for byte. Nothing is normalised and nothing is re-blessed during a run. The corpus is closed in both directions: a row here with no case in the validator is refused, and a case in the validator with no row here is refused. TWO ARGV PLACEHOLDERS EXIST AND ARE INPUT-ONLY: `{absent_registration}` and `{unreadable_registration}` resolve to paths OUTSIDE the repository, because a `service status` row needs a slot that does not exist and a slot holding undecodable bytes, and committing either would move the direct-include inventory while a file written under a candidate tree voids the battery that reads it. The substitution touches only the arguments a row supplies; the receipt it produces is still compared as parsed values with nothing rewritten.
